reviews.title: PS5 Lifesaver
reviews.comment: I got tired of having to delete older games or transfer them onto an external drive that I couldn't play games directly from so I finally pulled the trigger and got me this internal stick to save my games/movies. So far, so good. It was very easy to install and I haven't had any issues since installing it. The upload/download times are super fast. Excellent value for the money as these things can get pricey pretty quick...definitely would recommend if you're looking for a boost in memory for your PS5.

reviews.title: It's SSD memory.  It does what it says on the box.
reviews.comment: 4TB SSD memory with a bolt-on heatsink.  NVMe M.2 with PCIe Generation 4. Not the fastest memory on the market, or the biggest in terms of storage.  But it does the job.  It's a nice budget option for PC memory or even an expansion slot for a gaming console. If you like to watch movies, play video games, listen to music, or watch streaming TV (i.e. Netflix or Disney+) this can handle it.  You don't need the faster memory bus or "PCIe Gen5" technology unless you're getting into app development, GIS mapping & computations, molecular modeling, climate modeling, or AutoCAD engineering on a professional level - something where you're working with single files bigger than 250GB all day every day. I built a new computer from scratch about four months ago.  Threw THREE of these in there.  I'm using two for video game storage, and one as my main hard drive.  The CPU is water-cooled and there's a single 140mm radiator (exhaust) along with three additional 140mm case fans (2 intake, 1 exhaust).  Works great so far.  Just remember that if your PC or console comes equipped with its own heat sink, or if there isn't much space around the SSD slot, then you will need to use the SSD without attaching the included heat sink.
